story_summary: Test Login functionality for the dashboard
functional_intent: Verify that the login process authenticates registered users correctly, enforces input validations, protects against brute‑force attacks, and redirects authenticated users to the dashboard across web and mobile platforms.
in_scope_features: Email input field with format validation
Password input field with masking and non‑empty validation
Display of error messages for invalid credentials
Brute‑force mitigation (e.g., account lockout or throttling)
user_flows: Valid login: User loads login page → enters correctly formatted email → enters password → clicks login → credentials validated → redirected to dashboard.
Invalid email format: User enters malformed email → clicks login → receives email format error.
Empty password: User enters valid email, leaves password blank → clicks login → receives password required error.
Invalid credentials: User enters valid email with wrong password → clicks login → receives generic authentication error.
Brute‑force protection: User repeatedly submits invalid credentials → system triggers lockout/throttling → appropriate error shown.

risk_areas.description: Credential verification could be bypassed or exposed via insecure transmission.
Incorrect handling of input validation may allow login with malformed data.
Passwords must never be logged or stored in plain text during the test.
Error messages may be unclear or not displayed consistently across platforms.
Login response time could degrade under load or during brute‑force mitigation.

acceptance_criteria_breakdown.description: Users must be redirected to the Dashboard upon successful login.
testable_points: Redirect URL matches dashboard URL after successful authentication.
Redirect occurs within acceptable performance threshold (e.g., <2 seconds).

acceptance_criteria_breakdown.description: Passwords must be masked during entry.
testable_points: Password field input type is 'password' (masked characters).
Masking persists when toggling between platforms (Web, Android, iOS).

acceptance_criteria_breakdown.description: An error message must appear for invalid credentials.
testable_points: Generic error message displayed for incorrect email/password combination.
Message is visible, accessible (ARIA role), and not exposing which field is wrong.
Error message disappears after subsequent successful login.

acceptance_criteria_breakdown.description: The system must prevent "Brute Force" attacks.
testable_points: After a configurable number of failed attempts, account is locked or request rate is throttled.
Lockout state resets after defined cooldown period.

test_design_notes: Focus on cross‑platform consistency (Web, Android, iOS) for UI elements and error handling. Include security checks for TLS usage and ensure no sensitive data is logged. Simulate rapid failed login attempts to validate brute‑force protection without impacting shared environments. Leverage API interception to confirm password masking and token issuance. Validate accessibility of error messages. No test case details are included as per instructions.
